macro.story:
The tape is quietly constructive. SPY closed at 751.71, up 0.85% on the day and 1.95% over the past month, holding above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with buying volume dominant and MACD above signal. VIX sits at 15.8, down over 20% across the past 21 days, and index RSIs are mid-range (SPY 57.6, QQQ 52.2, Dow 60.5) — no overbought stretch, no washout. Under the surface there is tension: QQQ's MACD is still below signal and the Nasdaq 100 sector reading is neutral with a bearish momentum crossover, so mega-cap tech is not the leader today. Gold (-3.4% over 21 days) and silver (-7.7%) remain below their 50-day averages while DXY holds an uptrend — a validated dollar-up / metals-down dynamic. WTI is down 18% over 21 days but bouncing 5% on the week; the 10Y yield sits at 4.54% with the 2s/10s spread compressing to 0.33.

The prevailing sentiment in the tracked conversation leans firmly bullish and attributes the bid to two threads: record corporate insider buying in the tech sector and record Big Tech bond issuance to fund the AI capex cycle (Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, Meta, Oracle all cited). A parallel theme highlights US consumer credit falling for the first time since late 2024 and the odds of 2026 inflation above 4.5% collapsing from ~85% to 19% — the dominant view reads this as disinflationary and equity-supportive. One dissenting voice in the conversation is leaning bearish on financials and select single names (HOOD, JPM, ENB). This narrative is only partly consistent with the price data: insider-buying and AI capex are real drivers, but the sector tape shows Technology as NEUTRAL and Financials/Healthcare as the actual leaders today — the sentiment story may be lagging the rotation the sector data is already flagging.

Sector momentum reads Financials (score 9.8, RSI 64.8) and Healthcare (9.2, RSI 63.9) as HOT, both above their 50- and 200-day averages with bullish MACD. Utilities, Energy and Industrials are qualifying. Technology and the Nasdaq 100 sit neutral with bearish MACD crossovers — a caution flag on growth leadership. Materials, Real Estate and Consumer Staples are weak. The rotation radar is loud: Health Information Services, Diagnostics & Research, Drug Manufacturers, Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, Credit Services and Internet Content all show validated Early-Runway tailwinds, still early in their hot spells with top-decile relative strength.

Forward watch: whether Technology's MACD crossover repairs (a re-acceleration would broaden the bull), whether Financials/Healthcare leadership persists into next week's tape, and whether the 2s/10s compression continues — a flatter curve while risk assets rally is the tension worth tracking. Bull regime remains in force with SPY only 1.9% off its 52-week high.
